correctness.rationale: For scalar real affine f(x)=<a,x>+b on an entire real separable Hilbert space and signed ReLU parameter measures in the *joint* Euclidean unit ball, line restriction along a/||a|| contracts TV. In one dimension decompose w=0 mass as constant c and push the w>0,w<0 parts to signed kink measures alpha±(t) weighted by |w|; the parameter-ball condition bounds their first absolute moments by TV. Vanishing distributional second derivative of the affine target enforces alpha_-=-alpha_+, and first moments fix slope s=||a|| and intercept b-c. The Euclidean vector-measure triangle inequality gives TV>=|c|+2 sqrt(s^2+(b-c)^2) for arbitrary signed Borel measures, not just atomic networks. Convex minimization in c produces exact branches 2 sqrt(s^2+|b|^2) for |b|<=s/sqrt(3) and |b|+sqrt(3)s above; explicit antipodal ReLU kink atoms of mass ±s sqrt(1+t^2), with an optional flat c atom, attain both. Kink cancellation proves two atoms minimally below/equal threshold and three strictly above; constant and zero exceptions checked. Independent six-parameter SciPy scalar minimizations and direct pointwise ReLU representation checks agree to numerical tolerance, but do not replace the distributional proof.
residual_risks: Numerical finite diagnostics cannot replace analytic proof; scoped normalization and quantifiers are essential.
